characters.notes: 1) The band paints no sclera and no highlights (transparent), so the eye opening cannot be read from the band alone; it was measured on the band's own source frame (S2E19 t610.0, identified from the pipeline memory and confirmed visually) after fitting the band onto the frame (3.142 band px per frame px, overlap 0.949). The band is Battle City era; the owner's DK-first frames show the same eye design, so the shape carries over. 2) Units follow the brief except where the shader contradicts it: Tilt is (outer-inner cm)/8 under tiltY = _Tilt*x (both conventions round to -0.02 here); IrisScaleY is NOT a 1.0-1.25 stretch — the shader's p-space is 6x4 cm un-corrected, so a circular iris needs 1.5 and Téa's tall oval (visible h/w 1.31, lid-cut at the top) needs 2.0; with 1.15 her iris would draw 0.77 as tall as wide. H keeps the brief's height/8 and the measured corner split (corners in the upper 42 % of the eye) goes into TopBulge 0.85 / BotBulge 1.07; H*BotBulge = 0.49 touches the 4 cm quad's bottom edge, so the lower line may clip by ~1 px — if visible, drop H to 0.44 or BotBulge to 1.0. The eye is large (4.7 x 3.7 cm): other bands differ in scale too (Kaiba ~2.5 cm of eye paint, Mai 4.0, Yugi 5.9), and the owner has seen this band on the model. 3) At DK proportions (S1E25 frontal: eye 0.47 x 0.33 IPD, iris 0.30 IPD, h/w 1.05) the same preset would be W 0.30, H 0.32, Iris 0.19, IrisScaleY 1.6 — listed in case the reviewer prefers DK over the band's BC frame. 4) irisHex is the lit-frame cerulean (#50799C, six samples within ±3 across three episodes); the band's #3F4D74 is the same hue underexposed (sclera 142/255 in that shot; scaling by the sclera ratio gives #5E74AC). Expect the animated eyes to look brighter than the painted band. 5) The band lost the fuller eye's heavy outer-corner lash knot (it sits on the band's x=0 edge and was faded/classed as hair) and its upper-lash arc is faded alpha; the preset restores a 0.26-0.96 cm lash from the frame. Lash profile is really ~0.4 cm uniform with a 1.0-1.6 cm knot only in the last 0.6 cm at the outer corner; LashOuter 2.0 is a fit (the shader ramps smoothly). 6) The bangs strokes across the top of the band (y30-65) are hair, not brows; brows were measured in the neutral DK frame (thin, 0.3-0.4 cm, gentle arch peaking toward the outer end, dark ink not hair colour). 7) tea_mouth.png is the dark lip arc of an open 'o' (startled line in the source frame), 1.25 cm wide — not a resting mouth; resting values come from the closed-mouth DK frame (1.97 cm wide, flat line with ends 0.1 cm below the middle, hence RestCorner -0.1 rather than a cheerful smile; mouth W 0.12 is far below the catalogue's 0.22-0.38 because her drawn mouth is 0.26 IPD wide). Lids sit on the iris top in every frame, so despite the 'o' mouth the eye height is her normal open height. 8) Nose: the art draws a 2.2 cm sharp '>' bracket with a soft shade; Style 2 (point) is the closest; the shader cannot draw the long bracket line at any Size in range. 9) No eye is hidden, no opaque glasses; keepDecal false. Nothing in the repository or the Editor was modified; scratch files are in the session scratchpad only.

characters.notes: 1) Unit conversions follow the shader, not the brief's rules of thumb, where they differ: the eye quad's p space is 6 cm per x unit and 4 cm per y unit with no aspect correction, so (a) Tilt = corner height difference / 8 cm (brief said /6) and (b) a round iris needs IrisScaleY = 1.5 (brief range 1.0-1.25). IrisScaleY 1.54 here is the measured ry/rx 1.03 times 1.5; catalogue presets at 1.1-1.2 render irises ~30% wider than tall. 2) The band and the mouth decal are cut from S1E35 t284 (little Yugi facing Pegasus): a DETERMINED pose, white-flash washed. That is why the decal palette is lifted (iris #8077A0, ink 121,114,111); irisHex is the unflashed cel tone of the same shot and a neutral e002 frame, normalised to the sclera. If the reviewer prefers the band's literal colour, use #8077A0. 3) Expression bias: the steep upper lid toward the nose, the bold lower line and the inverted-U mouth (RestCorner -0.4 by the shader's 0.28 cm-per-unit corner drop; the brief's -0.15 'stern' would droop only 0.04 cm) are partly that frame's determination. The neutral e002 frames show the same eye construction with slightly less lid slope. 4) Brows are NOT in the band (the generator's brow band kept none; bangs cover them in the shot); they come from the frames: thin (0.14-0.18 cm), short (~2 cm), gently arched peaking outward, dark brown-black, sloping 17-28 deg inner-end-down in every frame read. The shader's brow tilt term is tiny (slope 0.176*Tilt), so +0.35 draws only ~3.5 deg; the measured angle would need Tilt ~2.1, and the shader comment and formula disagree on which sign lowers the inner end (y0 = ... + _BrowTilt*(-x)*0.14 raises x=-1, the inner end, for positive Tilt). Verify the sign in the Editor before raising it. 5) Lash/line weights: the cel quantiser thinned the ink (decal mid-lash 0.18-0.25 cm vs 0.36-0.45 cm in the source frame); values given sit between the two and are already below the catalogue's heavier defaults (Lash 0.055 default = 0.53 cm full at mid-lid). LowerLash 0.025 and Pupil 0.14 exceed the brief's typical ranges because Yugi's lower line is bold and his pupil ring is ~0.6 of the iris radius in the art. 6) Width: the character's right eye in the band is cut at x=61 by the bang strand and the window feather (visible 4.28 cm); W uses the complete left eye (4.54 cm). The source frame is slightly 3/4, so the true frontal width may be a few percent less. 7) Nose: the decal keeps only a small tan J-hook under the tip (Style 0); the source frame shows a long bridge-shadow wedge on the character's right side ending in a sharp tip (Style 1 would be the alternative). 8) The mouth decal is 512x256 and the rig's mouth quad is 4.4 cm tall (decal covers 4.2); mouth W assumes the 8.4 cm width. 9) No repository file was modified; frame grabs and crops live only in the session scratchpad.

characters.notes: 1) The band is NOT a neutral face: it is the label-upscaled anime frame S2E42 t316-319 (Mai vs Marik shadow duel), a pale colour-graded scene with her eyes widened in fear (H/W 0.72 vs 0.41 at rest in S1E06/S1E29). W, Tilt, lash, iris size, pupil and the hair layout come from the band; H, TopBulge, BotBulge, RestLid and Round were taken from the normally lit resting frame S1E06 t560.6 scaled by eye width (scale-free ratios), because a resting preset built on the band's H (0.32) and bulges (0.62/1.37) would ship a frightened face. If the reviewer wants the band literally: H 0.32, TopBulge 0.62, BotBulge 1.37, RestLid 0. 2) The band has no iris colour (the mauve iris body was stripped as skin; the scene is graded anyway); irisHex is the median of the S1E29 06:39-06:40 full-frame eye close-ups, #784370 (plum violet); Duel Links art is brighter (#AA5599). 3) Hair in the band: a cream lock with strand lines covers the inner half of her LEFT eye (viewer's right, x512-775 y144-322, its inner corner is hidden) and an olive shadowed lock sits over the outer top of her RIGHT eye (viewer's left); the dark wedge at x48-115 left of the right eye's sclera is that lock's edge ink, not the lash flick. 4) Unit conventions: the eye quad is 6x4 cm with uv 0..1 and no aspect correction, so vertical parameters are in 4-cm units; Tilt is +/-_Tilt at the two corners (0.15 = the measured 1.22 cm corner difference; the task's literal cm/6 reading would be 0.20), a round iris needs IrisScaleY 1.5 (the 1.0-1.25 guide range draws a wide iris), and Top+Bot = 2.0 is what H = height/8 implies. Mai's shape is a nearly straight slanted upper lid over a deep round lower lid, hence the unusual TopBulge 0.60 / BotBulge 1.55 split; her lash is thin over the iris (0.14 cm) and a heavy wedge at the outer corner (0.5 cm) with a long flick, which LashOuter 2.2 only approximates. 5) Scale caveat: the pipeline translated each eye to its anchor without rescaling, so the band's 3.55 cm eye is the source frame's zoom; her eye/IPD proportion in the anime (0.6) on the rig's 6.2 cm quad spacing gives the same 3.7 cm, so W 0.30 is consistent, but it is smaller than the catalogue's 0.38-0.44 style eyes. Band eye centres are 7.58 cm apart vs the rig's +/-3.1 cm quads. 6) Mouth decal is 512x256, not the 1024x512 the task states; measured at 8.4 cm per 512 px. Her mouth is genuinely tiny (1.62 cm, 0.45 of the eye width): W 0.10 is far below the catalogue's 0.22 minimum. OpenShape 0.55 and brow Tilt 0.15 are judgement calls documented in measurements (brow angles in the frames exceed the shader's range). 7) Nose Size/Shade are read from the frame's shadow wedge, not from a decal measurement. 8) mai_valentine_body.png is the FaceBake body-texture skin cover (a 2048 UV atlas), not standing art.

characters.notes: 1) The band is a 3/4-view Duel Links pose, not straight on: the far (viewer-right / character's left) eye is foreshortened and half under hair strands, the near eye's outer corner is open-ended (sclera unpainted where it was in shadow), and a hair-strand shade covers the inner-upper quadrant of both eyes. W/H/Iris come from the near eye, Tilt and the lid bulges from the far eye plus the straight-on e013 frame (both agree; the near eye's corner is ambiguous and reads flat to drooping). 2) No brows are painted in the band; brow numbers come from the e013 10:34-10:39 shot and the DL head: thin, near-straight, 12-16 degrees inner-end-low with the bend in the outer third, dark grey-brown (NOT the white hair colour, so hex is set). Brow Tilt 0.4 is on the catalogue's scale (brow_fierce = 0.35); by the shader's literal formula (drop = 0.28*Tilt of a 3.4 cm quad over a 5.4 cm brow) a 15-degree slope would need about 1.5, so the reviewer should check how Tilt is meant to map. 3) Lash, LowerLash and LipLine follow the task's stated scales (heavy / bold / thin) because the literal shader units (y unit = 4 cm for eyes, 4.4 cm for the mouth) would give values below the stated minimums (lash half-thickness 0.03, lip 0.01) even though the art is clearly heavy-lashed and thin-lipped; the cm values are in measurements. 4) IrisScaleY = 1.5 is deliberate: the band's iris fits a circle (0.4-1.0 px residual) and the eye quad is 6 x 4 cm with p = uv - 0.5, so a circle in cm needs y stretched by 6/4; if the host treats 1.0 as circular, use 1.0-1.2 instead. 5) Iris colour: the band's disc is a single flat desaturated tone #524C4C (82,76,76) with the whole eye region darkened (its sclera is 224 grey); the series frames measure a warm brown #856D57 / #856E5A. The series value is reported because the band's tone is a shading artefact of the cut-in and the character's eyes are brown in every anime frame checked; swap to #524C4C if the preset must match the painted band exactly. 6) RestLid 0.28 and the large iris reproduce the glare: the lash edge sits at or below the iris centre in both the band and the frames, hiding 55-60% of the iris; the shader's gaze offset (max 0.29 cm up) cannot place the iris that high, so the heavy lid is the closest rest state. 7) Mouth: the decal is 512x256 px, not 1024x512; it is a closed 3.9 cm lens with an asymmetric smirk (character's right corner higher) and a lower-lip stroke; the anime resting mouth is a much shorter smirk line (about 1.9 cm on the avatar scale), so W 0.23 follows the decal. OpenShape 0.2 because every open mouth in the sources (DL grin head, e013 frames) is a wide toothy grin. 8) Nose: the anime draws one long bridge line to a sharp point (Style 1, long so Size 0.65); the DL head instead draws a small dark triangle at the tip (Style 2) - pick 2 if the DL look is wanted. 9) hideEye none, keepDecal false: both eyes are ordinary; the hair strands in the band are hair, not eyewear. 10) e030/e031 sheets were scanned by hair colour but yielded no Yami Bakura close-up, so the e013 'Evil Spirit of the Ring' close-ups are the only series reference used; the fullframes montage (e013/e014) confirmed the same features across 20+ frames. Pupil 0.09 is the only value not measurable in the band (flat disc); it is 0.42 x Iris from the darker core visible in the 639 s frame.

Pupil 0.08 = (0.75 dark-core radius ratio minus the 0.13 limbal ring) x 0.13. BROW: thin straight brown stroke, 5 px (0.02-0.025 quad units, below the 0.05 floor -> 0.05), measured angle ~30 deg down toward the nose at rest (slope 0.6-0.8); on the documented scale that is the full 'angled in like anger' value 0.35, but note AvatarAnimeFace as written renders 0.35 as only ~3.5 deg (y0 = Tilt * -x * 0.14), so the measured V would need ~3 on that axis; hex #814F29 (daylight; #57320F purple-lit) — do NOT fall back to the hair-root colour, his hair is teal and the brows are brown. characters.notes: 1) THE CANON BAND IS NOT TRISTAN. Faces/tristan.png is Joey Wheeler's eyes cut from S3E10 at 10:10 (the pipeline memory lists 'Tristan S3E10 t610'; that frame is a Joey close-up, Tristan is a robot monkey in that arc). Proof: the band's ink registers onto that frame's eyes with IoU 0.61 (near) / 0.45 (far), the highlight, lower glint, lash and the bang strands crossing the near brow and falling between the eyes all coincide; Tristan's quiff never crosses his eyes. The band also carries no colour (sclera/highlights transparent, irises solid ink), so it could not give an iris colour anyway. Every number above is therefore measured from a genuine Duelist Kingdom-era Tristan frame (S1E39 1105.3 s: lit, near-frontal, stern rest face) scaled through the rig's 7.695 cm pupil spacing; the band should be rebuilt from that frame (or S1E39 1109.5 s) by whoever owns the decal tooling. keepDecal must stay false. 2) tristan_mouth.png (512x256, not 1024x512) is a smooth feathered V-chevron that looks drawn, not cut; it does not match the frame's resting mouth (a thin brown 3.8 cm arc, slightly downturned) and was not used. 3) Units: the task formulas were applied where given (W=/12, H=/8, Tilt=/6, Iris=/6, Pupil=/6, Lash half-thickness /6, mouth W=/16.8). The shader (p = uv-0.5 on anisotropic 6x4 cm quads) disagrees in places: it applies +-_Tilt in quad-HEIGHT units, so the measured 1.22 cm corner difference is reproduced by Tilt 0.15 rather than 0.20; the rendered centre height is H*(TopBulge+BotBulge)*4 cm, so with my bulges H 0.24-0.27 would reproduce the measured 1.34-1.54 cm; a circular iris needs IrisScaleY 1.5 on this quad (x unit 6 cm, y unit 4 cm), which is why 1.5 is given instead of the 1.0-1.25 hint; LipLine shader-true is 0.045 for the measured 0.22 cm line; Lash shader-true is 0.051 (mean) / 0.031 (thin part). The brow values were converted with the shader's actual factors because the task gives no formula: 15.7 deg slant -> _BrowTilt 1.6 (the rig's own 'angry' expression is 0.8 = 7.5 deg and 'determined' 0.45; Tristan's resting brows in the art are steeper than the rig's angry pose, his design has permanently knitted brows), mean 0.60 cm thickness -> 0.12 through the stroke taper, 0.9 cm arch -> 0.20. If the reviewer prefers the task's anchor scale, 0.35 renders only ~3.5 deg of brow slant. 4) Shape caveats the shader cannot express: the heavy lash is at the INNER corner (a 1-1.2 cm wedge) and thin outward (LashOuter 1.0 is as close as it gets; the stated 1.3-2.2 range does not fit); the upper lid is an almost straight 15-deg line and the eye hangs below the corner chord with a blunt outer end, hence BotBulge > TopBulge; the lash flicks ~1 cm past the outer corner (_Flick exists in the shader but not in this schema). 5) Iris: dark olive, not brown; main tone #514F3B, limbal ring ~#383628, light pool ~#9B8A73, small pupil (r 0.32 cm). Brows and lash ink #34322C (near-black cool brown), hair (130,109,77). 6) Confidence 0.55: geometry from one frame with 6-10 deg head roll (cancelled by averaging both eyes) and slight yaw; the far eye gives W 0.36 / H 0.16 vs the near 0.38 / 0.19; the sheets for e001/e002/e016 and the S1E35/S1E16/S1E2 frames confirm the narrow slanted eyes, dark olive irises, thick knitted brows and small stern mouth but were not measured to the pixel.

characters.notes: UNITS: I converted with the shader as written, not the task's rule-of-thumb. GridCard UVs are 0..1 and p = uv-0.5, so x is in quad WIDTHS and y in quad HEIGHTS (eye 6x4, brow 6x3.4, mouth 8.4x4.4 cm). Consequences: (a) eye Tilt is per corner (tiltY = _Tilt*x), so the outer-inner drop = 8*Tilt cm, not 6*Tilt; (b) length(ip) is anisotropic, so a round dot needs IrisScaleY = 1.5 (Iris*6 cm across, Iris*IrisScaleY*4 cm tall) - that is why IrisScaleY is above the 'typical' 1.25; (c) Lash/LowerLash are half-thicknesses in 4 cm units. EYE SHAPE: Rex's eye is not a normal almond - the upper lid is a straight slanted line from a sharp outer corner to the inner corner and the whole opening (sclera) hangs BELOW that chord (1.82 cm below vs 0.35 cm above at mid). Encoded faithfully as TopBulge 0.32 / BotBulge 1.68 at H 0.27 (opening 2.17 cm at mid, bottom at -0.45 units, just inside the quad). CAUTION - BLINK: the shader closes only lidTop toward the chord (lidBot moves only with _LidCurve, which the rig scales to <=0.4 during a blink), so with this BotBulge Rex's blink would close ~0.35 cm of a 2.17 cm eye, i.e. he will visibly not blink until the shader lets the lower lid rise (e.g. lidBot -> shutY with _Lid). Blink-safe fallback that keeps size and tilt but loses the straight lid: H 0.27, TopBulge 1.0, BotBulge 1.0. RestLid 0 because the straight lid is already the shape; the shock frame (eyes 1.4x taller) cannot be reached through RestLid anyway since all the opening lies below the chord. TILT SPREAD: band as painted 21.3 deg (0.23), de-rolled near eye 14.8 deg (0.16), far eye after roll+yaw ~20 deg, mean 17 deg -> 0.18 used; the frontal medium shot draws the eyes steeper (~30 deg -> 0.35) - a different drawing of the same model.
